source_discovery.function_contract_metadata: supported via a pinned Kani extension: Kani's proc-macro layer parses requires/ensures/modifies, the compiler preserves those parsed clauses in kani_metadata::ContractedFunction, and discovery carries them with proof_credit=false

accepted.functions: free functions with unit or supported scalar return types; selected primitive monomorphic generic instances remain allowed under the existing Kani-selection rule
statements: for _ in LITERAL..LITERAL with at most 32 iterations
expressions: +, -, * only inside executable if conditions; Verus must discharge fixed-width overflow/underflow
accepted.loops: literal ranges are exhaustively unrolled; this is not a general loop invariant or recursion theorem
accepted.assumptions: preserved at their source program point; for each user assumption, Verus proves that every otherwise feasible non-arithmetic path prefix retains at least one fixed-width input after the assumption
accepted.machine_arithmetic: Kani uses checked Rust overflow semantics at the pinned revision; translated +,-,* remain in executable Verus if conditions, where Verus requires overflow/underflow absence. Ghost arithmetic is rejected, and arithmetic-dependent assumption reachability is rejected rather than widened.
accepted.generics: source functions with unbounded type parameters only when Kani autoharness selected an explicit monomorphic instance and every selected type is in the supported fixed-width integer/Boolean set; the result is scoped to that concrete instantiation
accepted.function_contract_discovery: Kani compiler metadata preserves exact contracted-function identity/file/harness provenance plus Kani-parsed clause kind/expression records; the Verus bridge does not re-parse contract source attributes
accepted.function_contracts: restricted semantic lowering supports non-arithmetic requires predicates over supported scalar parameters; unit/scalar-return ensures may additionally contain exactly one u8/u16/u32/u64 +,-,* operation with one nonnegative integer literal on one side of a comparison. KVerus emits the exact fixed-width definedness guard into the Verus postcondition and records it as evidence. Scalar Kani result references are dereferenced into a named Verus result value; every accepted requires set is separately checked for existential satisfiability.

rejected: machine arithmetic in requires; signed arithmetic in contracts; nested contract arithmetic; variable-variable arithmetic; more than one arithmetic subexpression; arithmetic outside one top-level comparison; function calls, casts, old/history expressions, and syntax outside the declared Boolean/comparison grammar

non-scalar return contracts, result-reference types that do not match the function return type, bare/reference-valued result usage instead of scalar dereference, and arithmetic result expressions outside the guarded unsigned-literal subset
arithmetic in assert!/kani::assume, division/remainder, casts, arithmetic outside executable if conditions, and assumption non-vacuity paths that depend on machine arithmetic
function calls in the generated-source subset
references, raw pointers, slices, allocation and user ADTs
concurrency in the generated-source translator; reviewed Kani-selected functions may still bind to the separate existing Verus concurrency campaign through registry.json
generic trait-bound syntax, const generics, lifetimes, target-width generic arguments, dynamic loops, named loop variables and recursion
semantic_bridge.translation_trust: Structural lowering is an explicit trusted correspondence boundary and is regression-tested. Function-contract semantics come from clauses parsed by Kani's own proc-macro layer and exported through the pinned discovery evidence/metadata path; source attributes are stripped only to expose the decorated function body to the restricted parser. Requires arithmetic remains rejected because Kani evaluates a requires expression before kani::assume, so inserting a guard would change overflow behavior. In ensures, one unsigned fixed-width scalar/literal +,-,* operation may be represented in Verus only together with its computed Rust-definedness guard; the guard is part of the postcondition and evidence, while the body remains executable fixed-width Rust semantics. Every accepted requires set gets a separate Verus existential satisfiability proof before the contract-bearing function can receive proof credit. Scoped assumptions retain their existing Verus-checked path non-vacuity obligations. No general Rust-to-Verus or Kani-contract-to-Verus translation soundness theorem is claimed.
